newsitem.title: UK: Russia's Dubinin sees further MICEX expansion.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Dubinin sees further MICEX expansion.

text.p: Russia's central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Tuesday preparatory work was under way to further expand the regional network of the depository trading system of the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX).

"The opening of the new trading floors may eventually lead to the formation of a national stock market with an infrastructure that can also be used for transactions with non-government security," he said at a conference in London.

In 1996 MICEX's depository trading system was linked up with five new regional trading floors. The officially backed MICEX is looking for a new role as its share of the tightly regulated currency market is dwindling.
It is the official floor for the large and transparent government securities market, but wants to branch out into equities.

Trade in municipal and regional short term bonds (MKO-OKO) created a new market segment, although this segment constantly experienced pressure from the GKO-OFZ market owing to the latter's big volumes, high yields, liquidity and credibility, he said, but the volumes of MKO-OKO's operations on some regional floors grew rapidly.
